category_title: High school students with learning disabilities and ADHD who struggle to break down multi-step algebraic tasks
minimal_context: Marcia is multiplying the binomials (x + 3) and (x + 5) using only abstract notation during a one-on-one instructional session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's try multiplying (x + 3) and (x + 5) using only the abstract symbolism on your paper.

STUDENT: It’s so much more hard because it’s not broken up then. Like what I do is I see the blocks and I read it and I write it then I move it.

TUTOR: Just try to do it with the numbers this time.

STUDENT: But when it’s all numbers then I forgot where to break it up and what’s what.

TUTOR: Write down what you think the answer is.

STUDENT: Okay, I'll just multiply the x's and the numbers. It's x2 + 15. Is that right? I can't tell if it's right without the blocks.

options.A: Use a visual schedule that identifies the activities of the one-on-one instructional session and the reinforcers she is eligible to receive for contingent performance.
options.B: Implement a self-management intervention involving self-monitoring, self-evaluation, and self-reinforcement using a daily checklist during the one-on-one instructional sessions.
options.C: Set a standard of interacting with the student at a ratio of four positive interactions to one negative interaction during the one-on-one instructional sessions.
options.D: Allow the student to frequently move back and forth between the ALG blocks and the abstract notation when monitoring the accuracy of her solutions.
